page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Two portrait medallions side by side with legends around them, no text blocks. Below them one full-width column of running text (paragraph 1, then paragraph 2). No margin notes.

main_text.l: MENELAVS REX SPAR.
AGMEMNON REX MYC[?]
MENELAVS, Atrei (alij dicunt Plisthenis) & Aeropes
filius, in uxorem accepit Helenam formosissimā quidem mu-
lierem, attamē quæ bis rapta est, primùm à Thefeo, postea à Pa-
ride. Hic Menelaus regnauit apud Lacedæmonios anno mundi
2758. ante Christum natum 1204. aduersus Troianos bel-
lum gessit pro recuperanda uxore, quam non nisi capta Troia
recuperauit. bellum gessit decem fere annis. præterea conscen-
dens nauim in reditu, non nisi post octauum erroris annum pa-
triam attigit. Tantæ molis erat infame reducere scortū. scribit
nihilominus Dictys Cretensis non tam animo consternatum
fuisse Menelaum ob raptam uxorem, quàm ob Aetram & Cly-
menam, affines suas. Sustulit ex Helena Hermionem. Dares
Phry. Ouid. lib. 11. Metamorp. Cæterùm Menelaum Atrei fi-
lium Homerus scribit, Hesiodus autem, Plisthenis.
AGAMEMNON regnauit Mycœnis anno mundi
2768. ante Christum natum 1194. hic frater fuit Menelai: &
omnium consensu Græcorum dux præcipuus aduersus Troia-
nos declaratus est: classem habuit nauium sexaginta supra cen-
tum: uniuersa Græcorum classis erat nauium plus mille. Tan-
dem reuersus ab expeditione illa, & bello Troiano confecto,
ipse, insidiis Clytemestræ uxoris, ab Aegystho adultero interfi-
citur: Orestésque filius eius hanc iniuriā ulcisci-tur, interfectis
adulteris, matre scilicet Clytemnestra ac Aegystho. Euripid. in
Oreste, Seneca in Agamemnone. Dares Phrygi. Dictys Cre.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are copied from the engraved rings. The right legend is partly hidden by the curve of the medallion: "AGMEMNON" and "REX MYC" are my reading, and the end of the word is uncertain. Paragraph 1: "Clytemestræ" (paragraph 2) and "Clytenestræ" are the same name as printed. Some letters in the scan are faint, but the running text reads cleanly. No notes in the margins.
